status_summary: Executive Order 14190 (signed 2025-01-29) calls for a strategy to end federal funding or support for K-12 instruction it calls gender ideology or discriminatory equity ideology and for enforcement of civil rights and parental-rights laws. The race-focused guidance ran into court: a Maryland federal court ruled on 2025-08-14 that the Education Department's 2025-02-14 anti-DEI letter and its certification requirement were unlawful, and the Department withdrew its appeal on 2026-01-21. The gender-focused part has operated through funding conditions: HHS gave 46 states and territories 60 days on 2025-08-26 to remove gender ideology content from federally funded sex-education materials after ending California's grant, and the Justice Department opened a Title IX compliance review of a Michigan district's health curriculum on 2026-02-18. No national removal of these topics from public school curricula has occurred, and curricula remain largely a state and local matter.

timeline.event: President signs Executive Order 14190 (published 2025-02-03): within 90 days agencies are to recommend how to end federal funding or support for K-12 instruction involving gender ideology or discriminatory equity ideology, and it re-establishes the 1776 Commission. It creates no enforceable rights.

A New Hampshire federal judge issues a preliminary injunction barring enforcement of the Education Department's anti-DEI policy against members of the National Education Association, its New Hampshire affiliate and the Center for Black Educator Development; she declined to block it nationwide.

The U.S. District Court for the District of Maryland (Judge Stephanie A. Gallagher; Civil No. SAG-25-628, American Federation of Teachers v. Department of Education) enters judgment for plaintiffs on Counts One, Two, Three, Five and Six and for the government on Count Four, and vacates under 5 U.S.C. 706 the Education Department's 2025-02-14 Dear Colleague letter and its companion Reminder of Legal Obligations document, which carries the certification request.
timeline.source: U.S. District Court for the District of Maryland

timeline.event: HHS's Administration for Children and Families announces that 46 states and territories have 60 days to remove gender ideology content from federally funded Personal Responsibility Education Program materials or face withholding of funds; it had already ended California's grant.
timeline.source: HHS Administration for Children and Families

timeline.event: Education Department publishes final grant priorities that include returning education to the states and expanding education choice, and says it plans a later notice defining patriotic education.
The Education Department withdraws its Fourth Circuit appeal of the Maryland ruling that voided the 2025-02-14 Dear Colleague letter.

The Justice Department Civil Rights Division opens a compliance review of the Lansing, Michigan school district's pre-K to 12 health instruction on sexual orientation and gender identity, requesting curricula and lesson materials by 2026-04-06 and citing possible funding suspension or termination under Title IX if informal resolution fails; no conclusions had been reached.

The Education Department publishes a final supplemental priority and definitions on promoting patriotic education for discretionary grant programs (document 2026-10347); this is an adjacent grant-priority step and does not itself remove any curriculum content.

title: Remove critical race theory and gender ideology from public school curricula
uncertainties: The Foreword names critical race theory and gender ideology; the executive order uses different terms (discriminatory equity ideology, gender ideology). The New Hampshire ruling was read through news only; the Maryland order was read on a storage.courtlistener.com copy (it vacates both documents under the Administrative Procedure Act; it does not use the term K-12, so the K-12 limit of the certification rests on Education Week, and the accompanying memorandum opinion, including any First Amendment reasoning, was not read); Education Week says the Maryland ruling found both the letter and the certification unlawful, while the law-firm summary does not address the certification. The remedy label vacated matches the order's text. The ACF release states no deadline date; outcomes after the 60 days (other than California) were not identified, and the Yahoo report on Oregon and Washington gives no calendar date. The Lansing review is an information request, not a finding. The stage was moved from blocked to in_progress in review because the gender-related funding conditions continue to operate while only the race-related guidance was struck down. A search for 2026 curriculum actions beyond these was limited. The patriotic education priority (2026-05-22) was read as a Federal Register API abstract only.
